rows.meaning: every one; all of a group
rows.note: This is the all-purpose choice for every member of a group or the whole set.

example.english: All students have to hand in their homework.
example.jyutping: so2 jau5 hok6 saang1 dou1 jiu3 gaau1 gung1 fo3

rows.note: This is the all-purpose choice for saying that something is wholly or completely so.

example.english: I have no idea at all where they went.
example.traditional: 我完全唔知佢哋去咗邊。
example.jyutping: ngo5 jyun4 cyun4 m4 zi1 keoi5 dei6 heoi3 zo2 bin1

rows.note: Use this after an action verb when the action has been completed in full, as in 做晒 for “finish it all.”

example.jyutping: di1 gung1 fo3 ngo5 zou6 saai3 laa3

rows.note: Use this after an adjective when a situation has become completely that way, as in 靜晒 for “completely quiet.”

example.english: The streets outside are all quiet now.
example.jyutping: ceot1 min6 di1 gaai1 zing6 saai3 laa3

rows.note: Use this as the all-purpose choice for everyone in a shared group or audience.

example.english: All of you, listen to me first.
example.jyutping: daai6 gaa1 teng1 ngo5 gong2 sin1

rows.note: Use this when you want to emphasize every individual person rather than the group collectively.

example.english: All of them say it’s delicious.
example.jyutping: go3 go3 dou1 waa6 hou2 sik6

rows.note: Use this before a time expression such as 日, 晚, or 個星期 for the whole stated period.

example.jyutping: sing4 go3 sing1 kei4 dou1 lok6 jyu5

rows.note: Use this as the all-purpose choice for everything or all the things involved.

example.jyutping: so2 jau5 je5 dou1 zeon2 bei6 hou2 laa3

rows.note: Use this before a noun or activity when “all” means only or nothing but that thing.

example.english: I want nothing but coffee, not tea at all.
example.jyutping: ngo5 zing6 hai6 jiu3 gaa3 fe1 m4 jiu3 caa4

rows.meaning: the only thing; that is all
rows.note: Use this to say that nothing more exists or is meant, as in “that is all.”
